issue_context.title: Import cycle when adding plugins in scheduler NewRegistry
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:

When I add new plugins in [`framwork.NewRegistry`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/v1alpha1/registry.go#L57), there is an import cycle when compiling.

Suppose that we add the example plugin: `prebind` as following:

```
func NewRegistry() v1alpha1.Registry {
	return v1alpha1.Registry{
		// FactoryMap:
		// New plugins are registered here.
		// example:
		// {
		//  stateful_plugin.Name: stateful.NewStatefulMultipointExample,
		//  fooplugin.Name: fooplugin.New,
		// }
		prebind.Name: prebind.New,
	}
}
```
Then the file `pkg/scheduler/framework/v1alhpa1`(whose package is `k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/scheduler/framework/v1alpha1`) will import the package `k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/examples/prebind`. Howerver the `prebind` has already imported the package `k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/scheduler/framework/v1alpha1`, an import cycle occurs.

**What you expected to happen**:

No import cycle occurs.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

review_comments: I think we should move `registry.go` to `framework/` and only move the definition of `type PluginFactory = ...` to `framwork/v1alpha1/interface.go`.

I tried that, there is also an import cycle:
* `framwork/registry.go` uses `v1alpha1.PluginFactory`, then `framework` will import `framwork/v1alpha1`.
* `framwork/v1alpha1/framework.go` uses `framwork.Registry`, then `framwork/v1alpha1` will import `framework`

There is a lot of relationships between these types and interfaces: `Registry` -> `PluginFactory` -> `FrameworkHandle` -> `WaitingPod`, so we need to move `PluginFactory`, `FrameworkHandle`, `WaitingPod` and other related types/interfaces to a separate package(e.g. `framework/v1alpha1/types`). How about this? It might be better to keep it as the the PR is now.

All of the changes here are to remove the `NewRegistry` function from `framework/v1alpha1`. The function is at the moment empty and doesn't do much yet. We will provide a solution in the next step to define default plugins and apply plugin configuration. That solution will probably change `NewRegistry` and how it works. I would wait for that solution before making the changes proposed in this PR.
I agree with Bobby, we also need to think about a way to allow defining an order that the plugins in a specific extension point are executed (this is important for filter plugins).

When we created the configuration for plugins, we discussed the order of their execution. We tried to capture the final decision in [this comment](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/apis/config/types.go#L143). Here is a snippet:
```
Enabled plugins are called in the order specified here, after default plugins. If they need to
be invoked before default plugins, default plugins must be disabled and re-enabled here in desired order.
```

> When we created the configuration for plugins, we discussed the order of their execution. We tried to capture the final decision in [this comment](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/apis/config/types.go#L143). Here is a snippet:
> 
> ```
> Enabled plugins are called in the order specified here, after default plugins. If they need to
> be invoked before default plugins, default plugins must be disabled and re-enabled here in desired order.

I met the same problem when converting the binding function to a plugin, the default plugin is the default strategy. And if we run it first, it will use the default binding strategy for all the pods.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8aca2c148018770e4ad0f4b21d98a81ff714f731/plugin/pkg/scheduling/defaultbinder/plugin.go#L43-L57

 I think we could add another field `Priority` in the `Plugin` struct to solve this problem, and I created an issue https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/82050 for this proposal, 

```go
type Plugin struct {
	// Name defines the name of plugin
	Name string
	// Weight defines the weight of plugin, only used for Score plugins.
	Weight int32
	Priority int32
}
```

@bsalamat @ahg-g Yes, the function is empty now, it aims to solve import cycle for PR of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/80304(converting default sort plugin). I split it to two PRs because others might also need this PR to convert other default plugins. I'll send the PR for #80304, then we could figure out the problem and solution.
Just sent a PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/82204 for #80304 that depends on this PR to explain its purpose.

A good solution to move forward with for now is to create a ```default_registry.go``` under framework/plugins/, the file would include a function named NewDefaultRegistry similar to the one defined here that returns a registry instance with plugins created under framework/plugins.
Thanks for the suggestion! There is another import cycle when implementing #82204. I'll rethink it later.
Can you explain what import cycle the approach I am proposing introduces?

Sorry for misunderstanding, it is not introduced by your approach. 

When I implemented #82204, I found another import cycle, I just added a note in that PR. I have resolved in another way, although it smells a little bad.

This is too long for an import alias, but it seems that we don't have a better name for this.

The length of `frameworkv1alpha1` is a little long, but it only happens when both `k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/scheduler/framework` and `k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/scheduler/framework/v1alpha1` are imported in a same file.
